text:
lee_support: Customer ACME backfill failing, lots of indexer errors: "vector_dim_mismatch". Indexer expects 1024 but ingest shows 1536. Backfill job id: bf-2026-03-16-4. Started seeing failures ~1932101200. Can we triage?

maria_ml: do we know when the model was last changed for their workspace? any model-version tags on the payloads?

simon_eng: putting eyes on logs now. can you paste a sample error line and a sample request payload? also, how big are the batches?

lee_support: sample error from indexer logs: 
```
2026-03-16T22:14:11.342Z ERROR indexer: insert failed id=usr-78321 reason=vector_dim_mismatch expected=1024 got=1536 batch_id=bf-2026-03-16-4 shard=us-east-1
```
sample embed request we sent (trimmed): 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "model": "embed-opt-1536-v2", "input": ["doc text ..."], "client_meta": {"user":"acme","workspace":"acme-prod"} }
```
We started the backfill after export re-ingest scripts yesterday. Billing spike reported by finance.

deploy-bot: deployment notice: embed-service@deploy-2026-03-16T20:40:02 applied (release embed-opt-1536-v2)

maria_ml: aha — looks like customer historically used our embed-1024 model; ops must have switched the backfill to the new 1536 model. That would explain mismatched vectors. Two separate problems: during backfill some documents were produced with 1536 dims while the vector DB schema is still 1024.

tara_prod: quick mitigation steps: 1) pause the backfill queue (bf-2026-03-16-4) 2) set indexer to reject mismatched dims with clear error (so we don’t partially index bad rows) 3) run a dim-audit job on a sample of pending batches to get scope. @simon_eng can you flip the reject flag?

simon_eng: flipping indexer.enforce_dim_strict=true on staging/production flags now. Will emit metric indexer.dim_mismatch_count. Pausing queue — sending job kill for bf-2026-03-16-4 (graceful stop).

lee_support: customer is complaining about latency and partial results; they want a plan and ETA. Finance also flagged unexpected billing because some re-embeds already consumed tokens.

maria_ml: root cause analysis draft: 1) embed-service released embed-opt-1536-v2 at 2026-03-16T20:40 (deploy-bot). 2) backfill script was not pinned to a model or validated dims at ingest, so some workers used new model while others used older pinned docker image (race during rollout). 3) result: mixed-dim vectors ended up in the ingest queue -> indexer rejects.

lee_support: customer asks for repro steps. I'll paste a minimal repro we used: 
1) produce a batch with model embed-opt-1536-v2 via curl
2) send to ingest queue with same job id but via parallel workers (one running older image)
3) indexer rejects.

simon_eng: adding a concrete repro snippet: 
```
# produce 2 vectors with different models (simulate race)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-1024","input":["a"]}' | jq .data[0].embedding | wc -c
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-1536","input":["a"]}' | jq .data[0].embedding | wc -c
# then push both to the same backfill job id in parallel
```
This reproduces dimension mismatch in the queue.

tara_prod: long-term fixes: 1) enforce model-version tag on backfill jobs (immutable), 2) add a pre-ingest dim-check step that rejects/normalizes vectors before indexer, 3) make backfills idempotent so we can re-run without duplicate billing surprises, 4) provide a migrator service that rewrites vector DB schema if customer requests moving to 1536 (with cost estimate).

lee_support: customer wants immediate remediation: they'd accept either (A) convert their index to 1536 and finish backfill, or (B) re-run backfill pinned to 1024 and drop failed partials. Which is faster?

maria_ml: depends on data size. If <50M vectors, re-embed to 1024 might be faster (and cheaper) because converting old 1024 -> 1536 is non-trivial. If they want 1536 going forward, recommend a two-step: migrate DB schema to allow 1536 with explicit downtime window, then finish backfill. Need product signoff for schema change.

simon_eng: action items assigned: 
- simon_eng: enforce_dim_strict flag + metric (done) 
- tara_prod: draft backfill rollback vs migrate playbook, include cost estimate and migration runbook (ETA 6 hours) 
- maria_ml: run a sampling audit (10k vectors) to quantify mismatch ratio and report to customer (ETA 2 hours) 
- lee_support: customer comms template + offer to pause billing for re-embeds until we have plan (please coordinate with finance)

deploy-bot: indexer.metric.indexer.dim_mismatch_count incremented by 243 since 1932101200

lee_support: thanks all. I'll tell ACME we paused the backfill, we're doing a 10k sample audit next, and we may either roll forward to 1536 (if they approve) or re-run pinned 1024 backfill. Will update in 2 hours. :thumbsup:

maria_ml: +1. also adding a short-term guard: require model parameter present and add server-side dim header in embed responses so indexer can validate dims before enqueue. low-risk change -> will draft PR.

simon_eng: note for postmortem: make backfill jobs carry explicit model_sha and embed-service responses include vector_dim in response header X-Vector-Dim. That will prevent silent mixed batches in future.

tara_prod: logging note: include batch_id and worker_image_tag on every ingest log line so we can trace races.

lee_support: saved convo. will follow up with customer and escalate billing hold to finance.

[thread end]
